day_shape: 44 items: IDF strikes in southern Lebanon (Mansouri) and northern Gaza, Jerusalem Post reports Iran's new IRGC/military appointments include AMIA-linked figures, Iran International cites 916 executions since January, nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: Israeli strikes in Lebanon and Gaza
threads.summary: The IDF struck the southern Lebanese village of Mansouri in Tyre, while Palestinian media reported one dead and one injured in a strike on a vehicle in Beit Lahiya. IRIB reported the Mansouri strike and alleged Israeli forces were deliberately setting fires in south Lebanon forests, citing The Guardian.

threads.label: Iran post-war command reshuffle
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Iran's newly appointed military and IRGC leaders include sanctioned officials and figures linked to the 1994 AMIA bombing, filling posts vacated after Israeli and US strikes. A senior Iranian source told Reuters there were no US-Iran talks to extend the ceasefire because Tehran considered the deal to have no start date.

threads.label: Gaza Board of Peace plan claims
threads.summary: Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman claimed on X that the 15-point Gaza Board of Peace plan grants Hamas's military wing $160 million in cash, per Jerusalem Post. KAN News reported Hamas may receive up to $400 million in debt relief under the same plan, and the IDF disputed a separate Liberman claim that it ignored Gaza militants conducting a raid exercise.

threads.label: IRGC messaging via PBS interview
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB carried remarks by IRGC supreme commander adviser Mohammad Naqdi in a PBS interview, saying an Iran without missiles would be more dangerous and that Iran's 'atom bomb' is influence in peoples' hearts. Ansarallah political bureau member Muhammad al-Bukhayti told Defa Press Yemeni forces would target any Israeli military or intelligence presence in Somalia.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressures and environment
threads.summary: Iran International cited the Abdorrahman Boroumand Center reporting at least 916 executions in Iran since January, including 15 in August, and reported oil slicks reaching Qeshm mangroves and spreading toward Oman's coast. A separate Iran International Instagram poll indicated more than eight in ten respondents would leave Iran if given the opportunity.

Hanieh Sharifi in the snatch initially successfully cleared 91kg but failed on her next two attempts at 96kg and 99kg, finishing in seventh place. Sadeghzadeh made up for it in the clean and jerk. In the first lift she pressed 122kg overhead, failed to clean 126kg on her second attempt but successfully cleaned it on her third attempt, setting a 126kg record and winning the youth double gold

events.title_en: US human rights groups sue Trump administration over heavy sanctions against International Criminal Court — According to The Guardian, four major US human rights organisations have sued the Trump administration, saying the administration's sanctions against the International Criminal Court have effectively restricted victims of war crimes' access to justice
events.summary_en: US human rights groups sue Trump administration over heavy sanctions against International Criminal Court — According to The Guardian, four major US human rights organisations have sued the Trump administration, saying the administration's sanctions against the International Criminal Court have effectively restricted victims of war crimes' access to justice. After the International Criminal Court's investigation into the Zionist regime's crimes in Palestine, US sanctions against the body were imposed. The plaintiffs say these sanctions have caused accounts to be frozen, travel restrictions and pressure on lawyers and human rights activists and effectively punish those working to hold perpetrators of crime accountable.

events.summary_en: Video: 1,400 mokbs on the route to the shrine / Entry of 250,000 walking pilgrims by this morning — On 5 transport routes leading to the holy shrine of Imam Reza, 1,400 service-providing mokbs have been stationed to provide worthy hospitality to pilgrims of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Reza. By this morning, approximately 250,000 walking pilgrims have arrived at Mashad al-Reza and according to statistics, 700,000 other pilgrims are also en route. According to road police reports, travel to Mashhad has increased 26 percent and so far approximately 40,000 vehicles have entered the city.
